evidence: Ifat page: a Walashma ruler "gained an ascendancy over the Muslim kingdoms of eastern Shewa", Ifat flourishing "from 1285"; Marcus: late 13th-century "hegemony of Ifat"; Makhzumi deposition not mentioned.
Ramses XI page: civil wars, and at his death "Egypt passed to two new separate dynasties" (reign ends c.1077/1075 BCE); source2: Tanite north, Theban priests south from c.1076 BCE.
UNESCO says the capital "was abandoned after an invasion in 993", textbook says it collapsed under Rajaraja I c.993; neither mentions 614 or Aggabodhi II.
Osei Tutu "led their combined forces in a successful war against the Denkyera about 1698/99–1701", after Asante kingdoms merged with Kumasi; Golden Stool introduced.
Xin page: Wang Mang's "usurpation of power from the ruling Liu family constituted an interim"; Xin dated AD 9–25; regency, acting emperor and 6–7 CE revolts not in opened excerpts.
Vallat: "the first Epartid sovereigns reigned at the same time as the last 'Simaškian kings'" (transition ca.1970); Stolper: "not a sharp dynastic change", possible Gungunum break c.1925.
Tewodros page: "Not of noble birth, Tewodros came to the throne through warfare against the feudal chiefs", reign 1855–68; Gonder capital until 1855; Ras Ali 1853 not mentioned.
Bulatovich (second half of page): "In 1887, Menelik turned over Goma to Dajazmatch Tesemma", and the Goma resisted the Abyssinians; Britannica 'Oromo' is general only.
Tor: Sanjar escaped Ghuzz captivity 551/1156 and "in the spring of 552/1157, he died in Marv"; Khurasan then contested, later absorbed by Khwarazm.
Mahmud in 393/1003 marched into Sistan, defeated and carried off Khalaf; "Sistān now became a province of the Ghaznavid empire"; no siege mentioned.
Under Shalmaneser V Assyria "conquered the city of Samaria" (heading 722 BC); "Samaria itself became the centre of a new Assyrian province"; 720 date and Galilee not mentioned.
Britannica: decisive step "taken in 1271 when the Chinese dominion was given a Chinese dynastic name"; Iranica: civil war to 1264, empire "splintered in about 1261-2".
Cambridge summary: power divided among governors and warlords, "By 907 the remnants of T'ang control ... had been extinguished"; Britannica: Aidi "forced to abdicate to Zhu in 907".
Britannica: "In 961 Nicephorus Phocas ... reconquered Crete" and destroyed the Arab fleet; siege of Chandax and theme status not described; source2 not needed.
Grenet: "Eventually in 467 the Kidarites were expelled from their capital" and the remnant sent embassies to China until 477; how the remnant ended is not stated; Bivar silent.
UNESCO: Zapotec capital flourished "from the year 500 B.C to 850 A.D."; Britannica: Classic zenith "circa 500"; neither states a phase boundary at 500 CE.
Lodi page: Ibrahim's harshness led Dawlat Khan to invite Babur; "Ibrāhīm was killed at the first battle of Panipat (April 21, 1526)"; confederacy dissolved.
Marcus: "In 1270 a leading nobleman of the province of Shewa, Yekuno Amlak, rebelled", regicide of Yitbarek; Zagwe page: Yitbarek "was driven out and murdered".
Briant: "Byblos, Arados, and Sidon quickly surrendered", "Tyre defied him for seven months"; no year given, only placed after Issos (333); Sidon page silent on revolt and conquest.
Vriddhagirisan: war "broke out in 1673", Madura annexed Tanjore under Alagiri, Vijayaraghava perished; Maratha usurpation in "the early part of 1675" (1911 EB says 1674).
